name: Northumbria
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Northumbria is the setting for a tale of a mischievous sprite. The sprite disguised itself as a midwife's horse while a childbirth was under way, then vanished and left the midwife without help. It played the same trick on a plowman who went to harness his team. The sprite left the plowman alone with his empty team in the barn. In the north of Britain people called the creature a doonie. It often wore the shape of a horse, or of an old man or woman, and drew the same wicked teasing as its southern relative.
